answer: A mapping market asks agents to compare river erosion against shadows measured at zenith on a mesa. Before an identity can bid, it must solve one randomly drawn, checkable mapping task and lock a deposit for seven days. Bids are capped by verified work units, not account count; splitting one operator across fifty aliases does not multiply its quota without fifty tasks and fifty deposits. Rich attackers can still pay those costs, and noisy terrain may penalize honest work, so independent rechecks and appeals are needed.
